```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

projectData makes the objects in installed data packages available under the
names you expect, and reads each object only when you first use it. The normal
workflow has three steps:

1. **Install** the data package.
2. **Attach** it.
3. **Use** its objects, interactively or in a script.

Need another data package later? Attach it too. If the packages define the same
name, projectData asks you to decide which one you mean (see
[Conflicts](#conflicts)); it never picks a winner by order.

## 1. Install

Installing is ordinary R package installation and is not done by projectData. A
data package distributed as a tarball (for example from Zenodo) is installed
like any source package:

```r
install.packages("path/to/rnaseqData_1.0.0.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

To keep this vignette offline, the next chunk builds two tiny throwaway data
packages in a temporary library. In real use, skip this chunk and omit the
`lib.loc` argument below.

```{r fixtures}
library(projectData)
source(system.file("examples", "fixtures.R", package = "projectData"))

lib <- fixture_library()
fixture_package(lib, "rnaseqData", "1.0.0", lazy = TRUE, datasets = list(
  counts_rna = list(counts_rna = matrix(1:6, 2)),
  meta_rna   = list(meta_rna = data.frame(sample = c("a", "b")))
))
fixture_package(lib, "proteinData", "2.1.0", lazy = FALSE, datasets = list(
  counts_prot = list(counts_prot = matrix(7:12, 2)),
  meta_prot   = list(meta_prot = data.frame(sample = c("a", "b")))
))
```

## 2. Attach

`data_attach()` takes the name of an installed data package. It records what
the package contains and puts its objects on the search path under their own
names. This reads package metadata only: no data values are read, and nothing is
installed. Nothing is attached unless you call this function.

```{r attach}
data_attach("rnaseqData", lib.loc = lib)
```

## 3. Use

Use the objects by their ordinary names. The first use of an object reads it.

```{r use}
data_config(messages = TRUE)
counts_rna
```

The message says that local installed files were used and that nothing was
downloaded. The same code works in a script after the `data_attach()` call.

Attach another package whenever you need it. Objects already in use are not
affected.

```{r attach-second}
data_attach("proteinData", lib.loc = lib)
counts_prot
```

## Looking at what is available

Everything below reads only recorded metadata. It never opens any data.

```{r catalog}
data_catalog()[, c("collection", "exposed_name", "resource", "state")]
```

`state` is `unopened` until the object has been used, then `ready`. The
`resource` column is the loadable unit, which can differ from the object name.
A resource that produces several objects is opened once for all of them.

`data_info("counts_rna")` returns the full provenance row for a name: package,
version, installed location, source file, and how the mapping was determined.
`data_help("counts_rna")` opens the help page of the original topic in the
source package. It is separate from inspection and never runs implicitly.

## Loading individual objects

Attaching registers the package, and these functions then work on any registered
collection, attached or not. They take objects by explicit call, without relying
on names on the search path (the next section shows registering without
attaching):

```{r explicit}
data_get("meta_prot")                      # resolved like a bare name
data_get("meta_rna", collection = "rnaseqData")   # qualified by collection
get("meta_rna", envir = data_env("rnaseqData"))   # one collection's environment
```

`data_load()` opens resources eagerly, for predictable batch runs.

In scripts, `data_get()` is the most robust access path, because attached
bindings can be evaluated by IDE completion or previews (see
`system.file("ide-repro", package = "projectData")`).

## Inspecting a package without attaching it

`data_register()` builds the same inventory as `data_attach()` but exposes no
names. Use it to see what a data package offers before deciding to attach it.
A collection that is registered can later be attached by its id.

```{r register}
data_detach()
data_unregister(data_collections()$id)

fixture_package(lib, "rnaseqBatch2", "1.0.0", lazy = TRUE, datasets = list(
  counts_rna = list(counts_rna = matrix(101:106, 2)),
  meta_rna   = list(meta_rna = data.frame(sample = c("c", "d")))
))

data_register(c("rnaseqData", "rnaseqBatch2"), lib.loc = lib, id = c("batch1", "batch2"))
data_collections()[, c("id", "package", "version", "attached")]
data_catalog()[, c("collection", "exposed_name", "binding", "state")]
```

The catalog already shows the problem here: `counts_rna` and `meta_rna` exist in
both collections, so their `binding` is `ambiguous`. Registering does not change
the search path, and it reads no data.

## Conflicts {#conflicts}

When two attached collections define the same name, the name cannot be resolved
by order. Attaching still succeeds, and the catalog flags the conflict. Using the
bare name fails with an error that lists the candidates:

```{r conflict, error = TRUE}
data_attach(c("batch1", "batch2"))
counts_rna
```

There are three ways to resolve it, and they can be combined.

**Per-object preference.** Choose the collection for a particular name. This is
the right tool when several collections are equally important.

```{r prefer}
data_prefer("counts_rna", "batch1")
counts_rna
```

Other contested names stay unresolved until you decide them:

```{r prefer-others, error = TRUE}
meta_rna
```

**A primary collection.** If one collection should win *all* its contested
names, designate it. There is at most one, and a preference for a specific name
still overrides it. It can also be set when attaching:
`data_attach("batch1", primary = "batch1")`.

```{r primary}
data_primary("batch1")
meta_rna
```

**Suffix aliases and qualified access.** A suffix exposes every object in a
collection also as `<name><suffix>`, which is handy for keeping older code
working. Set it when you attach. Qualified access, `data_get(name, collection =)`,
needs no setting.

```{r suffix}
data_attach("rnaseqBatch2", lib.loc = lib, id = "batch2", suffix = ".batch2",
            replace = TRUE)
counts_rna.batch2
data_get("counts_rna", collection = "batch2")
```

Suffix aliases must be unique. A clash is reported when you attach, before
anything is changed. To clear decisions, use `data_prefer("counts_rna", NULL)`
and `data_primary(NULL)`.

## Cleaning up

```{r cleanup}
data_detach()
data_unregister(data_collections()$id)
```

`data_detach()` removes only the environment projectData created.
`data_unregister()` removes registrations. Neither deletes files or affects
objects you already hold.

## What this does not do

* Class compatibility, software versions, backing files, and platform-specific
  readers still matter; projectData does not guarantee reproducibility.
* Returned objects are shared references to one cached resource, not
  independent copies.
* Related tools: `conflicted` resolves conflicts between package exports and
  `library(include.only = )` selects exports. They work with exported data but
  do not provide collection inventory, deferred access beyond lazy data,
  format-specific restoration, or provenance.
